The '''2013 UEFA Europa League final''' was the final match of the [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League]], the 42nd season of [[Europe]]'s secondary club [[association football|football]] tournament organised by [[UEFA]], and the 4th season since it was renamed from the UEFA Cup to the [[UEFA Europa League]]. The match was played at the [[Johan Cruyff Arena|Amsterdam Arena]] in [[Amsterdam]], Netherlands, on 15 May 2013,<ref>{{cite news|title=Wembley, Amsterdam ArenA, Prague get 2013 finals |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0250-0c50f416ad08-db9153f27513-1000--wembley-amsterdam-arena-prague-get-2013-finals/ |website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=16 June 2011 |access-date=16 June 2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110618072033/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/aboutuefa/organisation/executivecommittee/news/newsid%3D1644074.html |archive-date=18 June 2011 }}</ref> between Portuguese side [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] and English side [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Chelsea won 2–1 to secure their first title in this competition.<ref name="guardian">{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/may/15/benfica-chelsea-europa-league|title= Chelsea's Branislav Ivanovic climbs highest to sink Benfica|date=15 May 2013|work=The Guardian|access-date=21 May 2013 }}</ref>

Chelsea were the first [[UEFA Champions League]] title holders to play in the following season's Europa League, after becoming the first Champions League holders to be eliminated in the group stage. With this triumph, they became the only Champions League holders to win the Europa League (no other team did so prior to 2024, when amended regulations meant this was no longer a possibility). Chelsea also became the fourth club, and first in England, to [[UEFA club competition records#List of teams to have won the main European club competitions|win all three major UEFA club titles]] at the time, having won the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] in [[1971 European Cup Winners' Cup final|1971]] and [[1998 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final|1998]], and still held the Champions League title won for the first time the [[2012 UEFA Champions League final|previous year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0250-0c50fd9b3a41-ad426c6c0241-1000--chelsea-join-illustrious-trio/|title=Chelsea join illustrious trio|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=15 May 2013}}</ref> Chelsea were also the first team since [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the [[1991 European Cup Winners' Cup final]] to win a major European final without making any substitutions.<ref>{{cite news |title=Torres far from feeling blue as he delivers epic performance [Champions in numbers (statistics box)] |author=Oliver Kay |newspaper=The Times No. 70886 |url=https://www.thetimes.com |date=16 May 2013 |access-date=16 May 2013}}</ref>

As a result of winning this competition, Chelsea secured a place in the [[2013 UEFA Super Cup]] against the winners of the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League]], Bayern Munich.

==Venue==
[[File:2012-13 Europa League final - Chelsea FC vs. SL Benfica, Amsterdam ArenA, kick-off.jpg|thumb|The match was played at [[Amsterdam Arena]] in front of more than 46,000 spectators.]]

The Amsterdam Arena was announced as the venue of the 2013 UEFA Europa League final on 16 June 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=Amsterdam ArenA to stage 2013 Europa League final|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0250-0c50f416ab1b-ad3a5a863e40-1000--amsterdam-arena-to-stage-2013-europa-league-final/|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |access-date=3 May 2013|date=16 June 2011}}</ref> The home stadium of [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] since 1996, it staged the [[1998 UEFA Champions League final]], where [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] beat [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] 1–0 for their seventh title, and was also one of the [[UEFA Euro 2000]] venues, hosting five games including a semi-final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2013/final/stadium/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130323012834/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2013/final/stadium/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 March 2013|title=Amsterdam ArenA|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |access-date=3 May 2013}}</ref>

The previous home for Ajax's European matches, the [[Olympic Stadium (Amsterdam)|Olympisch Stadion]], also played host to European finals. One-legged finals include the [[1962 European Cup final]], where Benfica defeated Real Madrid 5–3, and the [[1977 European Cup Winners' Cup final]], where [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] were beaten 2–0 by [[Hamburger SV]]. It also hosted the second legs of the [[1981 UEFA Cup final]], between [[AZ Alkmaar|AZ '67]] and [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]], and of the [[1992 UEFA Cup final]], between Ajax and [[Torino FC|Torino]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2013/final/previousfinalsincity/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130323012441/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2013/final/previousfinalsincity/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 March 2013|title=Amsterdam's historic finals|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |access-date=3 May 2013}}</ref>

==Background==
Benfica qualified for their ninth European final, the first in 23 years since their 1–0 loss to [[A.C. Milan]] in the [[1990 European Cup final]]. Previous appearances include back-to-back victories in the [[1961 European Cup Final|1961]] and 1962 European Cup finals (3–2 over [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and 5–3 over Real Madrid, respectively) and unsuccessful presences in five other European Cup finals – [[1963 European Cup Final|1963]] (1–2 to Milan), [[1965 European Cup Final|1965]] (0–1 to [[Inter Milan]]), [[1968 European Cup Final|1968]] (1–4 to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]), [[1988 European Cup Final|1988]] (0–0, 5–6 on penalties to [[PSV Eindhoven]]) and 1990 (0–1 to Milan) – and one UEFA Cup final in [[1983 UEFA Cup Final|1983]] (1–2 on aggregate to Anderlecht).<ref>{{cite web|title=Benfica's European final pedigree|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/025a-0ea906974e06-1da8fa39fa43-1000--benfica-s-european-final-pedigree/|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |access-date=10 May 2013|date=10 May 2013}}</ref>

Before this season, Chelsea had never reached a final of the UEFA Cup or UEFA Europa League. They previously appeared in two [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] finals in [[1971 European Cup Winners' Cup Final|1971]] (2–1 win over Real Madrid) and [[1998 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup Final|1998]] (1–0 win over [[VfB Stuttgart]]), and two [[UEFA Champions League]] finals in [[2008 UEFA Champions League Final|2008]] (1–1, lost 5–6 on penalties to Manchester United) and [[2012 UEFA Champions League Final|2012]] (1–1, won 4–3 on penalties over [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]).<ref>{{cite web|title=Chelsea's European final pedigree|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0252-0cd391c5eab5-a70c45d5c98c-1000--chelsea-s-european-final-pedigree/|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |access-date=9 May 2013|date=9 May 2013}}</ref>

The only previous meeting between Benfica and Chelsea in European competition was in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League]] quarter-finals, which the English won 3–1 on aggregate (1–0 in Lisbon and 2–1 in London) en route to the title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0250-0c50fd9b081a-685bb0ef8489-1000--benfica-meet-chelsea-in-europa-league-final/|title=Benfica meet Chelsea in Europa League final|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|date=2 May 2013}}</ref> 
Both Benfica and Chelsea finished third in the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League group stage]], and entered the 2012–13 Europa League in the round of 32.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/025a-0ea906131285-ceac08b6a6ac-1000--benfica-and-chelsea-to-meet-in-europa-league-final/|title=Amsterdam denouement for Benfica and Chelsea|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|date=7 May 2013}}</ref> It was the fourth time in the tournament's history that both finalists featured in the Champions League group stage earlier in the season, after [[2000 UEFA Cup Final|2000]], [[2002 UEFA Cup Final|2002]] and [[2009 UEFA Cup Final|2009]].

==Pre-match==

===Ambassador===
Former Dutch international [[Patrick Kluivert]], who won the [[UEFA Champions League]] with [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], was appointed as the official ambassador for the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2013/final/ambassador/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902234442/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2013/final/ambassador/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 September 2012|title=Ambassador: Patrick Kluivert|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations}}</ref>

===Officials===
On 13 May 2013, Dutch [[referee (association football)|referee]] [[Björn Kuipers]] was appointed to the final. He was joined by fellow Dutch officials Sander van Roekel and Erwin Zeinstra as [[assistant referee (association football)|assistant referees]], [[Pol van Boekel]] and Richard Liesveld as [[assistant referee (association football)#Additional assistant referee|additional assistant referees]], Berry Simons as [[assistant referee (association football)#Fifth official and reserve assistant referee|reserve assistant referee]], and German official [[Felix Brych]] as [[assistant referee (association football)#Fourth official|fourth official]].<ref name=officials/>

===Ticketing===
The international ticket sales phase for the general public ran from 3 December 2012 to 18 January 2013. Tickets were available in four price categories: [[Euro|€]]135, €100, €70, and €45.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2013/final/tickets/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121209033558/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2013/final/tickets/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 December 2012|title=Ticketing information|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations}}</ref> Each finalist club was allocated 9,800 tickets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sg.sports.yahoo.com/news/europa-league-final-ticket-allocation-beggars-belief-chelsea-120500550.html |title=Europa League final ticket allocation 'beggars belief' – Chelsea Supporters' Trust chair |publisher=goal.com |date=3 May 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131217222754/http://sg.sports.yahoo.com/news/europa-league-final-ticket-allocation-beggars-belief-chelsea-120500550.html |archive-date=17 December 2013 }}</ref>

===Team selection===
Chelsea's [[Eden Hazard]] was ruled out of the final after not recovering from a hamstring injury he suffered in Chelsea's 2–1 [[Premier League]] victory against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on 11 May.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/025a-0ea906ec3242-c1a73d68af50-1000--hazard-ruled-out-of-uefa-europa-league-final/|title=Hazard ruled out of UEFA Europa League final|date=14 May 2013|work=[[UEFA]]|access-date=15 May 2013 }}</ref> Chelsea captain and centre-back John Terry was also absent through injury.
Three players faced their former clubs: Benfica's [[Nemanja Matić]], who was transferred from Chelsea, and Chelsea's [[David Luiz]] and [[Ramires]], who were transferred from Benfica.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/printoutfiles/competitions/uefacup/2013/E/E_2010095_pk.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130612090650/http://www.uefa.com/printoutfiles/competitions/uefacup/2013/E/E_2010095_pk.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 June 2013|title=Match Press Kit|date=15 May 2013|work=[[UEFA]]|access-date=15 May 2013 }}</ref>

==Match==

===Summary===
[[Fernando Torres]] put Chelsea ahead in the 60th minute by rounding the goalkeeper and clipping in after being put clean in on goal by [[Juan Mata]]. [[Óscar Cardozo]] equalised with a penalty eight minutes later awarded after [[Eduardo Salvio]]'s header struck [[César Azpilicueta]]'s hand. [[Branislav Ivanović]] scored in the final minute of stoppage time with a header into the far corner from a Mata corner from the right to clinch a 2–1 win for Chelsea and with it their first Europa League title.<ref name="guardian"/>
